outputs.exact_statement:
There is a universal number $q>0$ such that, for every sequence satisfying $$\lambda=s^{-4},\qquad s\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad Zs^3\longrightarrow\infty,$$ and every choice of $n$ minimizing $E_n+\lambda n$, one has $$s^3(Z-n)\longrightarrow q.$$ The number $q$ is the exterior Coulomb charge of the unique classical solution, tending uniformly to zero at infinity, of $$\Delta F=4\pi k\bigl((F-1)_+\bigr)^{3/2}
 \quad\text{on }\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\},
 \qquad k=(5T/3)^{-3/2},$$ that is bounded above and below by positive multiples of $|x|^{-4}$ near zero. The density $k((F-1)_+)^{3/2}$ has bounded support, and $F(x)=q/|x|$ outside that support. Moreover, $$a_{\mathrm{TF}}=\frac37q^{-4/3}.$$

For every normalized unshifted $\delta$-state of finite particle number, $P_*\le C$. Fix $y\ne0$ and $C_0\ge1$. The data $X$ may be trivial. Otherwise, suppose that the initial cut, or finite sequence of cuts $(o_h,c_h)$, has total out support covered by at most $C_0$ cells $B_z$ with $$C_0^{-1}\le a_z/a_y\le C_0,
 \qquad
 \sum_h\bigl(|\nabla o_h|^2+|\nabla c_h|^2\bigr)
       \le\sum_z D_z^2a_z^{-2}\mathbf 1_{B_z},
 \qquad
 \frac{D_z^2}{a_zm_z}\le C_0\sqrt{P_*}.$$ Then, for the complete cut data, $$\label{eq:local-field-input}
 \left\|(\mathbb E[J_y\mid X])_+\right\|_2
       \le C(C_0)\frac{m_y}{a_y}.$$ The constants are independent of $Z$, the sector, the state, $y$, and $\delta$, apart from the displayed dependence through $m_y$.

The minimum $P(\lambda)$ is attained. Along [eq:scaling-regime], every minimizing index $n$ is eventually nonzero and strictly bound. For a normalized ground state $\Psi$ in that sector, put $D_0=E_n-E$. Uniformly over all these choices, $$\label{eq:rough-deficit} |Z-n|\le Cs^{-3},\qquad 0\le D_0\le Cs^{-7}.$$

There is a sufficiently large fixed $R_0$ such that, for every sequence of minimizing sectors and corresponding ground states in [eq:scaling-regime], $$\label{eq:exterior-cutoff} s^3\mathbb E_\Psi\#\{i:|x_i|>R_0s\}\longrightarrow0.$$

Let $j<J_*$ and let $A'\in\mathcal F_j$ have probability $p>0$. There is a normalized antisymmetric state $\Psi_{A'}$ in the same sector whose raw law is the raw marginal conditioned on $A'$ and whose form energy satisfies $$\langle\Psi_{A'},H_{Z,n}\Psi_{A'}\rangle
 \leq E_n+C r_j^{-2.02}\log^5(e/p).
 \label{eq:event-tilt-cost}$$ The constant is independent of the particle number, the number of observed arrays, and $D_0$.
